prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Move Sign-In After Pet Selection to Build Emotional Investment [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +15.0%, measured -10.4% ± 2.9%, after noise correction -5.6%, stopped early: sign_in worse
- round 1: Audio Chime and Desktop Active Badge on Completion [finish, notification]: predicted +5.0%, measured +0.9% ± 6.4%, after noise correction +0.2%, lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Split Card Layout with Direct Path Recommendations [choose_path, layout]: predicted +6.0%, measured -5.1% ± 2.2%, after noise correction -3.4%, lost: worse

By kind of change, after noise correction:
- choose_path, layout: -3.4% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, notification: +0.2% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: -5.6% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

One test is weak evidence. State a rule only when at least 2 tests of that kind agree after noise correction; otherwise say the evidence is still thin.

Previous lessons:
(none yet)

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Evidence for sign_in/reorder, finish/notification, and choose_path/layout is still thin as each has only one test so far.
Predictions were consistently too high across all round 1 tests compared to measured results.
